newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia sends in elite team for storm search.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia sends in elite team for storm search.

text.p: Malaysia sent in 24 members of an elite disaster team as the search intensified on Friday for more than 100 people missing from a deadly tropical storm that killed at least 106, police said.

The Special Malaysian Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) members left for remote Keningau in eastern Sabah state early on Friday, joining hundreds of other workers in their desperate search for survivors of the Christmas day storm.
SMART, drawn from police, armed forces and the fire department, was formed after the 1993 collapse of the Highland Towers condominium in Kuala Lumpur, which killed 48 people.
The team members, trained abroad in tunnelling and using tracker dogs, were deployed by helicopter to Keningau, located 150 km (95 miles) south of state capital Kota Kinabalu.
The small logging town was the worst hit by the storm with 102 bodies pulled from fallen branches, along riverbanks and the debris of their collapsed homes.
Other victims were found in the neighbouring towns of Papar, Tuaran and Kota Kinabalu.
Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad offered his condolences to families of the victims, saying the Sabah government and federal agencies have been directed to provide assistance.
"My wife and I wish to extend our condolences to the families of the victims and hope they stay calm and brave in facing this tragedy," the national Bernama news agency quoted him as saying.

Tropical storm Greg, which blew ashore in Sabah from the South China Sea at 70 kph (44 mph), triggered heavy rains and floods that swelled rivers to overflowing, downed power lines and washed out road and communications links.

A police spokesman in Kota Kinabalu said power had mostly been restored to Keningau, which is hidden under thick forest cover and nestled between mountains. "Power is OK but telecommunications is difficult," he told Reuters on Friday.
"We are trying to use our radio," he said.
He said about 230 people were involved in search and rescue efforts.
Officials said 500 houses in nine villages along the Pampang, Bayayo, Liawan and Sinagang rivers were washed away, leaving about 3,000 people homeless.

A majority of the dead were Filipino and Indonesian migrant workers living in accommodations built for them along the four rivers in Keningau by sawmill owners, the New Straits Times reported on Friday.
The Maritime Rescue and Coordination Centre in Malaysia said several ships were driven to shallow waters in the South China Sea by the storm but none were in real distress.
Sabah is a popular holiday destination but officials said Keningau, a logging town of 60,000, was not a regular tourist spot. So far, no foreign tourists have been reported to be among the dead.
It was one of the worst storms to hit Sabah in memory.
There was no immediate estimate of damage to crops. Sabah is a major grower of cocoa but Keningau only supplies a small portion of the crop, growers said.
